claim: Blood's GetSpriteExtents measures a sprite's top and bottom from the tile height and its y offset only, ignoring cstat 128, while the renderer honours bit 128. A sprite seated by its physics box is drawn sunk or floating. Town maps seat by what is drawn: their worst rates are 2.1% sunk and 5.6% squeezed.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/db.h:325-334 GetSpriteExtents; NBlood/source/build/src/engine.cpp:5401 (setup_globals_sprite1: cstat&128 in sprite drawing; :5140 is the same bit for voxels, classicDrawVoxel).

python -m tools.sprite_fit --rates over the town maps of tools/mine_city_assets.py TOWN_MAPS (E3M1, E3M2, E1M2, E1M4, E6M1, DWE3M1, DWE3M10), 2026-11-18, rerun 2026-11-26: sunk at most 2.1% (DWE3M1), squeezed at most 5.6% (E3M1).
use: Seat sprites by the drawn extent and run the sprite lint after placing or moving any sprite; read the list, not just the rate.

checked.how: db.h:325-334 GetSpriteExtents: top/bottom from tilesiz.y, picanm yofs and yrepeat, centred on z, no test of cstat 128. engine.cpp:5401 (setup_globals_sprite1) 'if (cstat&128) z2 += (yspan*yrepeat)<<1' is the sprite path; :5140 is in classicDrawVoxel, a voxel's.
